designOfTheInstrument.what: A register of beliefs the write path holds about its INPUT, derived by reading write paths, not by measuring output (ENFORCEMENT: code reading outranks output measuring).
designOfTheInstrument.method: Open each writer/planner file at origin/main, quote the decisive lines, classify the failure mode, then enumerate call sites for every guard before scoring it as a guard.
designOfTheInstrument.rankingRule: silent-* ranks above loud-throw; a guard that cannot fire ranks above a guard that fires wrongly
designOfTheInstrument.whatWouldMakeThisWrong: If a belief I record as unguarded turns out to be guarded at a call site I did not open, the row is wrong. Mitigation: every GUARDED verdict names the file:line of the guard AND I grep the call sites of that guard before scoring it. Rows I could not establish that way go in COULD NOT ESTABLISH, not into the register at lower confidence.

adversarialReviewOfTheMissionPremise.premise: Reading the engine write path predicts what breaks on an unprocessed county.
adversarialReviewOfTheMissionPremise.challenge1: A register of code beliefs cannot rank rows by POPULATION — how many counties actually violate each belief is a store question, and this lane is forbidden the database. Recorded as a structural limit: every row carries PRE-RUN DETECTABLE with the exact query, which is the deliverable's real value; the register predicts CLASSES, and the queries measure POPULATIONS.
adversarialReviewOfTheMissionPremise.challenge2: The engine is not the only writer. OPS-19 says the Factory is the only writer path. If the engine paths I read are retired-by-Factory, the register describes a dead path. Mitigation: I record for each row whether the module is imported by a live county script under packages/engine-core/scripts/, and I flag the engine/Factory seam (declared vintage vs latest tax_year) as its own row rather than assuming either side is canonical.
adversarialReviewOfTheMissionPremise.challenge3: Verified context handed to me could be stale at this SHA. I re-verified each of the four items against the SHA rather than restating them; findings that are now FIXED are recorded as findings.

earlyFindingsAtCp1: assertDidNamespace (packages/atoms/src/write-boundary.ts:74,78) returns early on an empty body.atomDid and on any id not starting with 'did:'. Every property-fact atomDid minted in fact-writer-ids.ts is a prefixed FNV token (cadroll_, lufact_, ownfact_, fhfact_, ...), so the guard is vacuous for that entire family. Call-site enumeration owed before this is scored.

resolveDeclaredCadVintage (packages/engine-core/src/cad-vintage/resolve-declared-cad-vintage.ts:25-41) has exactly 15 counties. 239 Texas counties throw FAIL CLOSED. Loud, so safe, but it is a hard statewide blocker and the map is hand-declared, mirrored by hand from LDT.

FOUR separate implementations of the same leading-zero normalization now exist: normalizeForJoin (fact-writer-ids.ts:165), normalizeParcelKeyToken (plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts:169), resolveCanonicalParcelKey's decimal-pad strip (parcel-write-identity.ts:126), and a SQL regexp_replace(prop_id,'^0+','') in parcel-geometry-resolver.ts:176. The SQL one is NOT equivalent: it has no all-digit guard and no lookahead.

verifyStoredParcelNodeAtom (parcel-node-atoms.ts:243) compares geometryStoreRef.propId against atom.parcelNodeId — two fields of the SAME body. Its docstring claims it proves the pointer resolves in txgio_parcel. It does not: it is internal consistency, which one upstream can satisfy alone.
